display.title: Episode 342: The Sound of the Shofar; The Storyteller Continues (Elul)
display.summary_short: The King in the Field, the Hakochainik march, Shema with a first-grade class, Rabbi Yehuda finally remembers one story, and the parable of the village bugle explains the shofar.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in Elul 5748, the month of mercy. Uncle Yossi recalls the Alter Rebbe's teaching that Hashem is like a king in the field who greets us with a shining face, so we should greet Him with simcha, and leads the Hakochainik march. After a recap of the story, a first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema. In the story, Rabbi Yehuda stays at the rich merchant's mansion through Shabbos still unable to recall any story; Reb Yitzchak says they must wait for the right time and sends him home in a coach, but moments later the coach stops and Rabbi Yehuda runs back: he has remembered one story. Then comes 'The Sound of the Shofar': quoting the Rambam, the shofar is an alarm, and a parable tells of a village boy who brings a fire bugle from the big city and blows it while houses burn, not knowing the bugle only calls people to fight the fire. So too the shofar calls us to act through teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. Candle-lighting time and the Dial-a-Jewish-Story line close the show.
display.lesson: The shofar is an alarm for action: hearing it is not enough unless we respond with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.
